characterizations.result_summary: Single Tg at 123.5°C observed for SMIA terpolymer, indicating homogeneous copolymer structure.

evidence.source_sentence: To verify there is no homopolymerization for St, the DSC curves were recorded. As displayed in Figure 2, only one single Tg appeared at 123.5°C in the DSC curves of the terpolymer SMIA, and the results agree with the empirical formula proposed by Fox et al. [20] which indicated that the structure of copolymer SMIA is relatively homogeneous.

characterizations.result_summary: TGA tests confirmed improved thermal stability of PVC composites with addition of ABS and SMIA, with Ti and T50 increasing for modified samples.

evidence.source_sentence: To confirm the thermal stability, we conducted the TGA curves of PVC, SMIA, and PVC/ABS/SMIA composites (Figure  10).

As for SMIA, a one-step degradation process was observed from $3 5 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$to $4 5 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } .$. The TGA curves of blends were similar to PVC, exhibiting a typical dehydrochlorination and carbon chain-breaking degradation process. When ABS (10 phr) was added to PVC, T and $\mathrm { T } _ { 5 0 }$increased from $2 6 1 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$and 304°C to $2 7 3 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$and $3 2 8 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$respectively. Importantly, $\mathrm { T _ { i } }$and $\mathrm { T } _ { 5 0 }$increased to $2 8 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$and $4 0 8 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$with the addition of SMIA. The thermal stability of the composites was significantly boosted by SMIA.

The tests were carried out under the tensile mode, at 1 Hz frequency and a heating rate of $3 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } /$min with a temperature range from $3 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$to $1 6 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } .$.

characterizations.result_summary: DMA tests performed on PVC/ABS/SMIA blends to measure glass transition temperatures.

evidence.source_sentence: DMA for the PVC/ABS/SMIA blends was performed on a DMA apparatus (Diamond-DMA, PerkinElmer, USA). The tests were carried out under the tensile mode, at 1 Hz frequency and a heating rate of $3 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } /$min with a temperature range from $3 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$to $1 6 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } .$. All of the samples had the following dimension $3 0 \times 1 0 \times 1 \mathrm { m m } ^ { 3 }$

characterizations.result_summary: SEM observation of impact fracture surfaces showed no obvious phase separation in PVC/ABS/SMIA composites, confirming good component compatibility, and morphology changes correlated with ABS/SMIA content and impact performance.

evidence.source_sentence: Phase separation was not observed in the scanning electron microscope images of composites, elucidating the outstanding compatibility of ABS, PVC, and SMIA.

The field emission SEM was used to explore the micromorphology of the impact fracture surface. As displayed in Figure  4a, the impact section of the composite material presents relatively flat with the addition of 6 phr ABS. The impact section of the PVC/ABS composite material contains well-distributed voids when the ABS is increased to 10 phr (Figure 4c). Some tree-root-like yielding fibers appear, which is a typical characteristic of toughness fracture. The fracture surface is not uniform at 12 phr (Figure 4d).

To deeply understand the impact performance of PVC/ABS/ SMIA composites, SEM images were acquired. As shown in Figure $^ { 6 , }$the boundary between the two phases was not found, and no obvious phase separation occurred.
